chunks: A group of scholars narrated to us from al-Talaqbari, from Ali ibn Habashi, from Ja'far ibn Malik, from Ahmad ibn Abi Naeem, from Ibrahim ibn Salih, from Muhammad ibn Ghazal, from Mufaddal ibn Umar, who said:

I heard Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) say: 'When our Qaim arises, the earth will shine with the light of its Lord, and the people will become needless [of sunlight]. A man will live long in his dominion until a thousand males are born to him, and no female is born among them. A mosque will be built on the outskirts of Kufa with a thousand doors, and the houses of Kufa will be connected to the river of Karbala and to al-Hira, so that a man will set out on Friday on a white mule intending to attend the Friday Prayer but will not be able to reach it in time.'
ai.seo_question: What are the signs of the earth shining and the lifestyle during the rise of the Qaim according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This narration from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Kitab al-Ghayba* outlines the physical and demographic transformations characterizing the reign of Imam al-Mahdi (a.s.), emphasizing divine light (*nur*) illuminating the earth as a sign of universal justice. The specific mention of a male-only population and extended lifespans reflects traditional eschatological interpretations of a purified era, while the urban expansion of Kufa underscores its centrality as the political and spiritual capital of the Mahdist state.
